nodes.label: actor-ts Working Standards
nodes.rationale: One file holds every convention for humans and coding agents alike, so a standard is discoverable in one place rather than re-derived from the diff history.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits policy
nodes.rationale: type(scope): subject with small focused commits, each keeping typecheck + test green so a bisect never lands on a broken tree; the body explains what and why, issues referenced as #NNN.

nodes.label: Commit identity pinning via environment variables
nodes.rationale: Tooling has been observed substituting a work address at commit time, and a wrong author only surfaces afterwards in the log; GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* outrank both --local config and -c user.email, and the values are read back out of git config so the recipe works unchanged in a fork.

nodes.label: develop / main / features branching model
nodes.rationale: develop is the integration branch and main holds releases only; every unit of work gets a features/ branch, so no change lands on develop without passing through a branch.

nodes.label: Always merge --no-ff, never rebase
nodes.rationale: History stays a true graph; it is never rewritten or flattened, in both directions (features to develop, develop to main).

nodes.label: Agent commits locally, human pushes
nodes.rationale: Nothing is pushed by the agent, so a wrong author or a bad commit is always still fixable by rewinding the branch; the single exception is cutting a release.

nodes.label: Pre-1.0 SemVer release strategy
nodes.rationale: Patch is fixes only, minor may break, 1.0.0 is the API-stability commitment; releases are cut on a release/vX.Y.Z branch, tagged vX.Y.Z and published as a normal Latest GitHub Release.

nodes.label: Re-measure comparison benchmarks at release time
nodes.rationale: environment.actorTsVersion comes from package.json and the docs tables label their columns with it, so a release that skips re-measuring ships figures attributed to a version that never ran; bump first, then measure, so results carry the new version and a clean commit rather than -dirty. Version labels belong in the docs tables and RESULTS.md, never in README.md (#1322).

nodes.label: Pre-1.0 hard cut for breaking changes
nodes.rationale: No deprecation cycle is required pre-1.0: remove or replace an API directly, flag it BREAKING in the CHANGELOG with a one-line migration note, and update every in-repo caller (examples, tests, docs, benchmarks) in the same change.

nodes.label: 1:1 bilingual Starlight documentation
nodes.rationale: English docs under docs/src/content/docs/ are mirrored 1:1 under de/; every content change updates BOTH languages, code samples stay identical and prose is translated. The i18n label tracks translation work.

nodes.label: Bot-maintained README test/coverage badges
nodes.rationale: A CI workflow pushes the badge numbers directly to develop, measured with the quarantined multi-node suites skipped, so hand-edited figures are overwritten and differ slightly from a local full run.

nodes.label: Verification gates before every commit
nodes.rationale: typecheck, typecheck:dev, bun test with a coverage floor, smoke, examples, benchmarks, DevTools UI and security scanning — each gate exists because a distinct class of defect is invisible to all the others.

nodes.label: typecheck:dev — the caller's-side compile
nodes.rationale: The only gate that sees the library from a caller's side: an exported class narrower than the interface it implements still satisfies `implements`, and an exported type whose properties are all optional is satisfied by nothing. Neither shows up in bun test (which transpiles without checking) or bun run typecheck (which never compiles a call site). Green since #540.

nodes.label: Coverage floor gate (aggregate + per-module)
nodes.rationale: Two floors from one --coverage run: the aggregate 80% from bun's `All files` row, and src/cluster/ + src/persistence/ at 90% from lcov as sum(LH)/sum(LF) per prefix — a rollup of per-file percentages would average a ten-line barrel against a thousand-line coordinator. Module floors live only in scripts/coverage-gate.mjs, deliberately: an env override in a workflow is a second place the number lives and a way to loosen the gate invisibly.

nodes.label: Coverage ratchet policy
nodes.rationale: A floor may be raised, never lowered silently. The aggregate was 89 until 83b0a4af dropped it to 80 for the worker-thread quarantine, with the reasoning living only in a commit message; both floors are now pinned from below by tests/unit/ci/CoverageGate.test.ts so lowering one means editing that test, in the same commit, on purpose.

nodes.label: ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS quarantine
nodes.rationale: Bun on GitHub's hosted runners cannot respawn functional worker threads after the first worker test, which also starves LeaseMajority's lease arbitration into a false split-brain; three suites are therefore skipped in test.yml, multi-runtime.yml and publish.yml. A local bun test runs them; a green CI check says nothing about them (#538).

nodes.label: Repeat-run flake hunting (test:stress)
nodes.rationale: Loops the suite N times and aggregates failures by test identity, splitting flaky from consistently failing. It drops ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS from the child environment by default — a harness that inherited it would report a reliable pass rate over exactly the tests known not to be reliable (#290).

nodes.label: Cross-runtime smoke gate
nodes.rationale: tests/smoke/cases/*.mjs run on Bun, Node and Deno. A case must release every handle on every path: a socket abandoned on a timeout keeps Deno's event loop alive and the run hangs after its last green line with no exit code, so the gate stops being a gate (#1196).

nodes.label: Examples manifest gate
nodes.rationale: Every standalone example is classified in tests/examples/examples.manifest.json as runnable-with-an-output-substring or skipped-with-a-reason, and the runner fails when manifest and tree disagree in either direction. The output assertion is not decoration: `exited 0` is also what a failing example does, so a runnable case without an expect would gate on nothing.

nodes.label: Benchmarks compile + smoke gate
nodes.rationale: The build tsconfig excludes benchmarks/, so nothing else catches an orphaned benchmark; typecheck:bench plus bench:smoke make benchmarks part of the adoption sweep for a breaking change, exactly like tests and examples.

nodes.label: Nested, un-hoisted DevTools UI toolchain
nodes.rationale: devtools-ui/ is deliberately not a bun workspace — hoisting would put @angular/core in the root node_modules and in Dependabot's view of a manifest that ships two runtime dependencies, and Angular pins a TypeScript the library does not use (#483). typecheck skips the UI half locally and fails hard under CI, which keeps a fresh clone working.

nodes.label: check:ui source-hash staleness gate
nodes.rationale: src/devtools/generated/UiAssets.ts is generated but committed, and a stale one is valid TypeScript, so nothing else notices. The check compares a source-hash rather than bundle bytes, because bytes vary with OS and Bun release; review is therefore the only thing that ever looks at the embedded payload, which is why .gitattributes gives the file a plain textual diff.

nodes.label: Two DevTools UI test runners with disjoint patterns
nodes.rationale: The framework-free half runs under bun test from devtools-ui/tests/*.test.ts; the Angular half runs under Vitest in jsdom from *.ng-spec.ts. The suffix is not a style choice — bun test collects *.spec.ts anywhere in the tree and would try to run specs needing Vitest and a DOM, so renaming them back breaks the root suite (#487).

nodes.label: CI-side security scanning with one local half
nodes.rationale: lint:audit reads bun.lock deliberately: GitHub's dependency graph resolves only the ranges in package.json, so Dependabot and dependency-review-action are blind to the shipped closure. Suppressed advisory IDs live in the script AND in SECURITY.md, with tests/unit/ci/SecurityPolicy.test.ts failing if the two sets differ.

nodes.label: Runtime portability behind src/runtime abstractions
nodes.rationale: Code must run on Bun, Node >= 24 and Deno; runtime-specific primitives (HTTP serve, sockets, workers, SQLite) live behind small abstractions in src/runtime/ and auto-detect at startup.

nodes.label: Optional peer dependency declaration policy
nodes.rationale: Lazy import() with a clear install error, declared in peerDependencies + peerDependenciesMeta.optional, then a SECOND time in exactly one of root devDependencies (justified by a test importing the real module and asserting the shape the adapter destructures) or tests/integration/brokers/package.json. A peer in neither context is the defect (#676): the structural stub standing in for its types is checked against nothing and no gate notices. Three silent traps: bun add no-ops on an existing optional peer, a package shipping no types needs its @types/*, and a root devDependency enters bun audit's surface.

nodes.label: Every match arm delegates to a private onXxx handler
nodes.rationale: Keeps the matcher a scannable dispatch table rather than logic. Applies wherever a match dispatches an incoming message, event or command; exempt are matches on internal state or that compute a value in a helper.

nodes.label: Measured-hot-path switch exemption
nodes.rationale: Building a matcher and one closure per arm is free at one call per request and is not at one per actor lifecycle. The exemption is per-site and evidence-carrying: the site must name the benchmark and the measured delta, and that comment is the token the conformance sweep (#494) recognises. Two sites qualify today (ActorCell.handleSystemCommand, BoundedMailbox.enqueue).

nodes.label: interface for contracts, type for everything else
nodes.rationale: An interface states a contract someone implements and extends reads as a hierarchy where an intersection only reads as conjunction; a data shape states a value's layout, and there type composes with the union aliases the project already uses. A function-typed property is not a function head.

nodes.label: Discriminated unions as named variant types
nodes.rationale: Each tagged union is a union of named members, never an inline object-literal union; variants are PascalCase(kind) plus a role suffix matching the union, and handlers take the named variant type rather than Extract<Union, { kind }>.

nodes.label: The discriminant field is always `kind`
nodes.rationale: `type` collides with the type keyword; `kind` is the single project-wide convention, including the WebSocket/wire protocols of the examples.

nodes.label: Pass the actor class, not a closure around it
nodes.rationale: spawn(() => new MyActor(), 'x') is a leftover from the Props era and reads as noise; actorFactoryOf does the wrapping. The factory form is for constructor arguments only, and per-actor configuration is the third argument, ActorOptions, never a closure.

nodes.label: Spell out abbreviations in identifiers
nodes.rationale: Full words everywhere including locals, params and kind string-literal values. Two exceptions only: single-letter loop/lambda/catch vars, and names mirroring an external API or an established domain acronym (nats.js ack/nak, prom-client inc/dec, amqplib noAck, PubSub, K8s, AMQP, MQTT, SQL, S3, DNS, CBOR).

nodes.label: HOCON keys through ConfigKeys with layered precedence
nodes.rationale: explicit options > HOCON > built-in defaults, layered with mergeOptions where undefined on a higher layer means 'not set' and falls through rather than shadowing. A key in reference.conf must be reachable from ConfigKeys and read by something in src/, else NoDeadConfigKeys.test.ts fails; adding a key nothing reads is not an option.

nodes.label: Angular templates always live in a separate .html file
nodes.rationale: Markup and logic are read, reviewed and edited by different motions. An inline template pushes the class off screen, has no HTML tooling, and puts HTML inside a template literal where a stray backtick or ${ surfaces as NG1010 nowhere near the cause — which has happened here twice, both times from a backtick inside an HTML comment. styles may stay inline.

nodes.label: Four-place constant placement rule
nodes.rationale: Checked in order: XOptions.ts default/bound, stays where it is (a closed list of six kinds), src/<subsystem>/Constants.ts, src/util/Constants.ts. A Constants.ts imports nothing from its own subsystem so it is cycle-free by construction; declarations move with their JSDoc, as const and explicit annotations, because dropping them is how a pure move silently widens a type.

nodes.label: XOptions family — three exports per configurable thing
nodes.rationale: XOptionsType, XOptionsBuilder and XOptions (both the accepted-input union and the value alias). There is no separate 'Settings' concept. Naming lockstep with no divergence: builder method withX, field x, HOCON leaf x.

nodes.label: XOptionsValidator — fail-fast validation at consume time
nodes.rationale: Validation runs once, at consume time, on the merged settings, so builder, plain object and HOCON are all covered and cross-field rules see final values. Helpers take only the field name (typo-checked against XOptionsType) and are a no-op on undefined; rejections throw OptionsError, distinct from BrokerOptionsError and ConfigError.

nodes.label: A builder is structurally its settings
nodes.rationale: OptionsBuilder.set writes each field as an own enumerable property, so consumers read the argument directly with no resolve helper. Keep the union in the signature — a methods-only builder is not assignable to a bare XOptionsType under the TS weak-type check. Never nest a builder into a call; assign it to a contextual local first.

nodes.label: Issue-first workflow
nodes.rationale: Check for an existing issue before starting; open one first otherwise, for traceability, using the matching template. Close via `Closes #NNN` in the commit body — GitHub resolves it once the commit reaches develop, the default branch, so there is no release-window in which to reconsider.

nodes.label: Comment on the issue whenever the work changes course
nodes.rationale: The commit message records what was done and why; it is a poor place for what turned out to be wrong on the way there, and it is invisible to anyone reading the issue later. Worth a comment: a stale report, a failed obvious fix, a bound that changed after measuring, a scope move, or a verification step that proved nothing.

nodes.label: Issue label taxonomy
nodes.rationale: priority/severity tiers plus security, i18n, infrastructure, dependencies, production-goal and the standard bug/enhancement/documentation; audit-catalog items carry the [Security] / [Feature] title prefixes.

nodes.label: production-goal label as a gate
nodes.rationale: It is a gate, not a batch marker, so it belongs on any issue that blocks or defines the path to production regardless of which review found it — filtering on it should answer 'what is still between us and running this for real', which is why it is applied to existing issues rather than duplicating them.

nodes.label: Security-first posture
nodes.rationale: Cap untrusted input (WebSocket / wire-frame size limits), never trust client-supplied integrity fields, use crypto-grade randomness for wire identifiers; a security-relevant change gets a Security CHANGELOG entry and a severity: label.
